hardest_risks: [WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] The glass wall is architectural, not a missing feature. It is not that Microsoft has not yet shipped a lensing brush; it is that the backdrop sampler lives in the out-of-process system compositor, which by design never hands pixels to the app (CreateHostBackdropBrush: 'The app cannot read the pixel data back'), while the shader engine lives in the app's D2D device and can only see images the app owns. No future Windows App SDK version plausibly changes that boundary, so there is no 'wait for 2.1' hedge.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] The rescue path makes things worse. Windows.Graphics.Capture would deliver desktop pixels, but the price is a user consent prompt at first run, the graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder restricted capability in the manifest (a Store certification conversation), SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) which blanks the app in the user's own screenshots and Teams shares, one frame of latency on every glass surface, and continuous full-screen GPU work. Shipping that to satisfy a visual requirement is a defect, not parity.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] Even the blur-and-tint fallback is not under the app's control. DesktopAcrylic is suppressed by the user's Settings > Personalization > Colors transparency toggle, by Battery Saver, and by power policy, falling back to FallbackColor - a solid fill. So the surface the whole app is made of can go opaque on a machine the owner never touched, which is precisely the 'flatten translucent material into a solid fill' failure PA-0001 names as unacceptable.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] The terminal and the glass are in tension. The one credible embedded-terminal option renders through the Windows Terminal DX backend in a swapchain, and microsoft-ui-xaml#5025 reports CompositionBackdropBrush cannot sample over a SwapChainPanel - so a terminal panel sitting on a glass surface, or glass chrome layered over the terminal, is a second unsolved compositing problem on top of the first.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] Text forces an early irreversible fork. Parity-grade line breaking and measurement point at Win2D CanvasTextLayout; the 1029 UI contract records and the control-shaped parts of the app point at XAML. Choosing wrong early means either rebuilding every control by hand on a canvas or discovering mid-port that XAML cannot hit the measured metrics.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] Caption buttons on the leading edge require abandoning the system title bar entirely (SetBorderAndTitleBar with hasTitleBar:false) and reimplementing drag, double-click-to-maximise, Snap Layouts on maximise hover, and per-monitor DPI hit-test geometry by hand - a known source of long-tail Windows bugs, and the traffic-light-derived layout constants have no analogue to re-derive from.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] Self-exclusion from screen capture is a real product regression with no workaround. WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE is required to stop the backdrop feeding back into itself, and it makes the window absent from Snipping Tool, PrintScreen, OBS, and Teams/Zoom screen shares. Users of a coding-agent tool screenshot transcripts and share screens constantly. The macOS original has no such cost. The only alternatives are an infinite mirror, or enumerating Z-order and capturing each window behind you individually with CreateForWindow and compositing them yourself - which is racy and absurd at 60fps. Surface this to the owner before committing, because it is a visible-to-users consequence of OD-0003 and it is not reversible inside the chosen stack.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] The monitor-wide yellow recording border. GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired=false is documented as ignored unless GraphicsCaptureAccess.RequestAccessAsync(Borderless) succeeds, which 'displays a prompt to the user' and needs graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder declared in a package manifest. If that path does not open silently for an unpackaged desktop process, the app either ships with a permanent recording border around the user's entire display, or ships as MSIX with a restricted capability and a first-run consent dialog. Either is a product-visible deviation from the macOS build. This is probe 1 and it is the single highest-value thing to settle.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] Backdrop lag against exact alpha. The lensed/blurred regions come from asynchronously delivered capture frames and are one to two frames behind; any genuinely clear region of the same window is composited by DWM with zero lag. During a window drag the two halves of the same material visibly disagree, and macOS never shows that seam because the compositor samples in-band. Whether it is perceptible enough to fail a side-by-side capture check is probe 2.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] The UI Automation and input-plumbing iceberg. 3827 requirements and 1029 UI contract records on a bare canvas means writing the virtualized list, IME composition, selection, focus, context menus, tooltips, IDropTarget, per-monitor-v2 DPI, high contrast, AND the entire IRawElementProviderSimple/Fragment/FragmentRoot tree with control patterns for every hand-drawn control. Direct2D gives none of it. This does not appear in any of the 12 constraints and I believe it is the largest single line item in the project.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] The terminal emulator. There is no SwiftTerm equivalent in C++. libvterm has a different state machine and no selection, reflow or scrollback UI; anything else is writing a VT parser. ConPTY handles the pty, but SwiftTerm 1.20.0 parity is a per-escape-sequence audit of a multi-month subproject, and the docs warn that servicing both ConPTY channels from one thread deadlocks.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] Live resize with springs still running. WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE hands control to a system modal loop that does not return until the gesture ends. Workable via a USER timer armed on entry, or a composition-swap-chain-to-redirection-surface switch, but every framework that has tried this has a long issue thread about it, and the spec asks for spring animations held THROUGH the resize, which is the hard version.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] @MainActor has no enforcement in C++. 256 confinement sites become convention plus debug asserts. TokenLedger's lock-free design and the sessionEpoch / finishingTurnID / unsentSessionID invariants depend on it, and a missed dispatch fails silently and intermittently rather than loudly.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] Even with total pixel control, Liquid Glass's exact algorithm is unpublished and PA-0001 confirms the source has no fallback to copy. Convergence is empirical against side-by-side captures. Native D3D is the only stack where that iteration is possible at all, but 'we can iterate toward it' is not 'zero guesswork' as OD-0003 asks, and the owner should hear that distinction stated plainly.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] The Parsec virtual display adapter on this machine. WGC delivers frames on the D3D device you created the frame pool with; if the captured output lives on a different adapter than your render device, you eat a cross-adapter copy every frame. On an AMD integrated GPU with a Parsec virtual display present, adapter selection and multi-monitor spanning are not hypothetical.

[Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), with DirectWrite for text, HLSL for the material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, and ConPTY for the terminal.] HDR. The capture docs note content may not be DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM on Windows HD color and recommend DXGI_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_FLOAT end to end plus tone mapping. The glass pipeline would need an HDR path or would wash out on HDR displays.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] Desktop-backdrop refraction is impossible, and the source makes it the DEFAULT look. WindowBackdrop's no-wallpaper branch is bare glassEffect over the desktop with only a 0.26/0.18 scrim, and because that window-level surface is transparent, all 18 inner glass sites inherit the limitation. Only the isSolid (>=0.98) branch or a fully opaque wallpaper gives the app its own backdrop, and those are exactly the settings where the source itself drops glass for a plain fill. So the shader path covers the configurations where glass matters least. This is the top risk and it is not fixable within the stack.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] The two glass mechanisms are mutually exclusive on the same pixels, and there is no blended middle. Configuration (a) TransparencyLevel=Transparent gives a sharp, unblurred desktop and no material at all; (b) AcrylicBlur gives a DWM-blurred desktop that Skia cannot touch, so specular edges and tint must be drawn on top as flat app art with no relationship to what is behind them; (c) an app-drawn opaque or wallpaper base gives the full shader material but no desktop. The owner's field evidence - 'nearly transparent over the DESKTOP with desktop widgets legible through it' AND 'edge refraction with visible chromatic fringing' - describes a combination that is (a)+(b)+shader simultaneously, and no configuration provides it. Blur radius is at least controllable if the DComp backdrop graph is authored directly rather than using Avalonia's hardcoded WinUIGaussianBlurEffect, so 'legible through it' is reachable; the fringing is not.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] The DXGI Desktop Duplication escape hatch costs the app its own visibility. WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE is documented as making the window 'not appear at all' outside a monitor, and it is honoured by BitBlt, DDA, Windows.Graphics.Capture and DWM thumbnails alike. For a tool whose users demo agents, pair-program and file screen-recorded bug reports, permanently vanishing from Teams, Zoom, OBS and the Snipping Tool is a product regression that may be worse than imperfect glass. This trade must go to the owner explicitly, not be made by an engineer.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] D3D11-texture-into-Skia interop is unproven in Avalonia. If the DDA path is taken, the captured texture must reach Skia through ANGLE's EGL_ANGLE_d3d_texture_client_buffer or the Vulkan backend's external-memory import, neither of which Avalonia exposes as a supported API. This is the single largest technical unknown in the assessment, it sits on the critical path for the primary weighted criterion, and it would be maintained against Avalonia internals that carry no compatibility promise.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] Spring animations held during live resize. Windows resize is a modal WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE loop; Avalonia's resize smoothness on Windows is the least-verified item here, and a full-window glass surface re-sampling every frame during a drag-resize is the worst possible load to put on it, on an integrated Radeon, with a Parsec virtual display adapter in the mix. SpringEasing itself is fine; sustaining it through resize is not demonstrated.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] Per-frame snapshot cost for 22 glass sites. Every SkSurface.Snapshot is a GPU texture copy. Sharing one snapshot per GlassEffectContainer (spacings 2, 2, 8 give three natural groups) should hold it to a handful per frame, but Chrome.swift:219 already records that a window-sized glass surface is a full-window sample every frame on hardware far better than this target. Unmeasured.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked has no Windows equivalent. DPAPI CurrentUser and Credential Manager both stay available while the workstation is locked. C7's 'equally unavailable while locked' requirement cannot be met, and the retained UserDefaults migration fallback must be actively refused rather than allowed to become the normal path.

[Avalonia UI 12.1.2 (current stable, Sept 2026) on .NET 10, rendering through SkiaSharp 4.152.x / Skia, with HarfBuzzSharp shaping, the Avalonia composition renderer, and Win32/WinRT interop via Win32Properties and MicroCom.] SwiftUI view-body re-expression is the bulk of the schedule. Avalonia has no declarative view-diffing equivalent; 1029 UI contract records become Panel/Layoutable subclasses with MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride. This is predictable, low-risk work, but it is large, and underestimating it is the most likely way the port misses its date even if every hard constraint is satisfied.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Self-capture backdrop side effects. Using WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE to stop the glass feeding back on itself makes the whole app invisible to Teams, Zoom, OBS, PrintScreen and the port's own e2e screenshots - for a coding-agent app that people screen-share and file bug reports about, that is a product regression, and it is the price of desktop lensing on Windows regardless of stack. Without it, the glass mirrors itself.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Fidelity gap that no amount of shader work closes: the captured backdrop is the last composed desktop frame (one frame stale, so the glass smears during window drag and live resize) and it contains windows stacked ABOVE the app as well as behind it, which macOS's in-compositor sampling never does. Exact parity with the field capture, including chromatic fringing at the border, is achievable in the shader; exact parity of WHAT is sampled is not.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] The embedded terminal. SwiftTerm is a shipping, mature VT emulator with a pty; Qt has no equivalent, and the credible Qt6+ConPTY projects are young single-maintainer repos. Writing or hardening a VT parser, screen model, scrollback, selection and mouse reporting is a multi-week item with a long tail of conformance bugs, and contract section 10 forbids the escape hatch.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Spring animations during live resize. Windows' modal resize loop blocks the GUI thread; Qt's animation driver and the render thread's sync point behave differently there than under macOS live resize. This is the most likely place where 'looks identical in a screenshot, wrong in motion' bites, and it is hard to fix once the architecture is set.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Type. Losing the macOS system font forces re-derivation of 430+ font sites and the .font(.chat...) scale against a substitute, and because text metrics feed layout, every measured UI contract record downstream of text shifts. Qt gives precise measurement tools, which helps, but the parity baseline for text has to be re-established rather than transcribed.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Toolchain cold start on this machine. No MSVC, no CMake, no Qt. The WinRT capture path additionally requires MSVC because C++/WinRT is not supported on MinGW; Desktop Duplication is plain COM and would build under MinGW, which is worth knowing if MSVC install size becomes an issue.

[Qt 6.11 (current shipping release; docs served as 6.11.1/6.11.2), C++ with QML/Qt Quick on the RHI scene graph, Direct3D 11 backend on Windows, plus direct Win32/DXGI calls for anything Qt does not wrap.] Licence mechanics rather than licence compatibility. LGPLv3 requires dynamic linking (or shipped object files) plus relinking and installation information, so the installer must keep Qt as DLLs and the About box must carry the LGPL text and notices; GPL-only Qt modules and the GPLv3 Qt Installer Framework must be avoided or accepted deliberately. Compatibility with an AGPLv3 application is not the problem; forgetting the relinking obligation in the installer is.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] The window-level glass has no API - only a screen-capture compositor. Every frame the app must capture the desktop, crop to its own window rect across DPI and multi-monitor boundaries, and redraw. Any latency shows as the backdrop lagging behind the window during a drag, which is the most visible possible failure of the exact thing OD-0003 protects. There is no fallback: DWM acrylic flattens to a solid colour on deactivate, which is the forbidden outcome.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] setContentProtection is required to stop the capture feeding back on itself, and it permanently prevents the user screenshotting or screen-sharing the app. For a developer tool whose users demo and file bug reports with screenshots, that is a serious product regression traded for a visual effect.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] The in-window refraction rests on unspecified, non-interoperable Blink behaviour (w3c/svgwg#1142; WebKit bug 245510 shows the other engine does not do it). Chromium could change or optimise it away in any release. The Electron pin becomes load-bearing for the app's visual identity, and every upgrade needs a side-by-side visual gate.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] Per-frame cost at 1320x860 on an AMD integrated GPU is unmeasured. The structural fact is bad: Chromium recomputes backdrop-filter only on invalidation, and .interactive() plus a live streaming transcript invalidates continuously - exactly the full-window-resample-every-frame cost Chrome.swift:219 already flags on far stronger hardware.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] Per-window renderer multiplication. Main plus settings plus up to six docked panels plus pop-out heads means many renderer processes, each needing its own glass surface and, on the capture route, its own capture consumer - there is no way to share a GPU texture between renderers.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL is not expressible. Node's documented Windows behaviour makes SIGTERM and SIGKILL both an abrupt forced kill, so the one-second graceful window simply does not exist, and 13 supervised provider CLIs lose their chance to flush and exit cleanly. Fixing it properly needs GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent or Job Objects via a native addon - which drags MSVC back into a toolchain that currently needs no compiler.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] Main-actor ordering invariants crossing an async IPC boundary. sessionEpoch, finishingTurnID and unsentSessionID are the named likely breakages, and they fail as rare interleaving bugs in a streaming transcript - the hardest class of defect to find with the e2e harness.

[Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node), TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js, electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater] Live-resize rendering stalls. Windows' modal move/resize loop is a known Chromium-hosted-window problem and collides directly with the requirement that spring animations keep running during resize.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] Desktop-backed Liquid Glass is unreachable by construction, not by effort: the web platform's backdrop is the Backdrop Root, and the only alternative, DWM Acrylic/Mica, is blur-and-tint with no lensing, specular edge or pointer deformation. Under OD-0003 this ends the evaluation.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] The two glass halves are mutually exclusive here: the transparent controller background that any desktop show-through requires is the same setting that breaks backdrop-filter in WebView2 (WebView2Feedback #4945, open since 2024, 'never worked'), so the stack cannot even combine system acrylic behind the window with SVG-displacement glass inside it.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] The lensing path that does exist is single-engine and unspecified: backdrop-filter with url() SVG filters is Chromium-only and, per w3c/svgwg#1142, not interoperable and not in the CSS spec. The app's entire surface treatment would rest on an unspecified Chromium behaviour delivered by an Evergreen runtime that updates itself under the app.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] Ordering invariants: Tauri documents that rapid successive events may be processed out of order by async listeners, against a source whose TokenLedger deliberately omits locking because main-actor confinement guaranteed order.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] Live resize: spring animations held during resize, over a transparent WebView2 window whose transparency already needs a documented resize workaround, on an integrated GPU rendering a full-window filter.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] Per-window cost: floating panels (three a side on a 16-inch display) plus pop-out head panels, each as a real window, each a WebView2 controller, while 13 CLIs stream concurrently.

[Tauri 2 (Rust core + wry/WebView2 on Windows), with window-vibrancy 0.8 for window effects] kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked has no Windows counterpart; DPAPI/Credential Manager remain readable while the workstation is locked.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] The desktop backdrop is unobtainable. Flutter has no API that yields DWM-composited desktop pixels as a texture, and `BackdropFilter` is documented as filtering 'the existing painted content' of the Flutter scene. The app's own source (`WindowChrome.swift:116-117`, `WindowBackdrop` in `Chrome.swift`) makes the desktop the window's base surface with a user-facing transparency slider, and field evidence shows desktop widgets legible through the window with chromatic fringing at the border. This is not an accent that can be dropped; it is the product's surface, and OD-0003 forbids substituting it.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Window transparency on Windows has never shipped. flutter/flutter#71735 has been open since 2020-12-04 with the desktop lead stating the Flutter view cannot be made transparent. Impeller/Vulkan becoming the Windows default in 3.47 likely makes the DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea hack worse, because Win32 Vulkan surfaces conventionally expose only VK_COMPOSITE_ALPHA_OPAQUE_BIT_KHR. Without a transparent view, even the capture escape hatch degrades from 'see the desktop' to 'paint a stale copy of the desktop'.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Multi-window is still experimental. 3.47 ships only popup, tooltip and dialog windows; `RegularWindowController`/`runWidget` remain `@internal` behind a main-channel feature flag. Three docked floating panels a side plus pop-out head panels either wait on an unreleased API or use `desktop_multi_window`, which gives each window its own engine and isolate and thereby destroys the single-actor ordering guarantees that C3 identifies as a correctness invariant. This is the risk that silently converts a low-translation-cost port into a high one.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Impeller on Windows is six weeks old as the default and is breaking the exact surfaces this app depends on. flutter/flutter#192918 (OPEN, 2026-09-17) has `BackdropFilter` under Windows Impeller erasing all content drawn before it in the same pass when offscreen MSAA is unavailable (D3D11 FL 10_0 / GLES 2.0) - a capability class a Parsec virtual display adapter can plausibly land in. flutter/flutter#191468 had DXGI shared-handle external textures crashing under Impeller on 3.47.0, fixed on main only. Betting a 3827-requirement parity port on a renderer this new, on the one platform that got it last, is a schedule risk independent of the glass question.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Live-resize animation fidelity. Constraint 9 requires springs held DURING live resize. The Windows embedder blocks in WM_SIZE waiting for a frame at the new size; desktop resize jank is a long-tracked problem (#44136) and a full presentation stall after a resize-handshake timeout was filed 2026-09-10 (#192537). Springs surviving an edge drag on an integrated Radeon is unproven.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Terminal dependency depth. `flutter_pty` 0.4.2 is ~20 months old, self-described as experimental, with no documented ConPTY behaviour; `xterm.dart` parity with SwiftTerm 1.20.0 is unmeasured. The contract forbids replacing the embedded terminal, so this dependency is load-bearing and thinly maintained.

[Flutter 3.47.2 stable (Dart 3.13, Impeller/Vulkan Windows embedder, native Win32 runner)] Subprocess semantics loss. `Process.kill` ignores the signal on Windows and terminates via TerminateProcess, so the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL gradation and the `getpgid(pid)==pid` group-kill condition must be rebuilt on Job Objects through FFI. Reachable, but it is bespoke native code in the part of the app that supervises 13 vendor CLIs.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Liquid Glass over the desktop is unreachable by design. WPF never possesses the pixels behind its window, and the one API that does (CreateHostBackdropBrush) refuses to hand them back and refuses custom shaders. Nothing downstream in this stack fixes that, so the field evidence of desktop widgets legible through the window and chromatic fringing at the border cannot be reproduced.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Even the app-drawn half is unreachable at fidelity. Lensing the live transcript or the Wallpaper layer behind a glass panel needs the app's own rendered output as a per-frame texture; WPF exposes no such handle (RenderTargetBitmap is a synchronous re-render), and ShaderEffect can only sample the element it is attached to.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] The two escape hatches are mutually exclusive with each other and with transparency. D3DImage needs hardware rendering, AllowsTransparency forces the layered-window GDI present path, and HwndHost (the Composition island, and the Windows Terminal control) is documented as not displayable at all when AllowsTransparency is true and as always drawing on top of WPF content otherwise.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Silent shader failure on exactly this hardware class. 'If a computer has more than one video card, the behavior is defined by the least capable video card' plus 'if a valid PS 3.0 shader is loaded on a computer that does not have hardware support for PS 3.0, the shader is ignored' with no exception, on a machine with an integrated Radeon and a Parsec virtual display adapter, means the glass could vanish on the owner's own PC with no error.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Pixel Shader 3.0 is a 2004 instruction set. Refraction with chromatic separation, an adaptive tint derived from the backdrop and a specular edge in one ps_3_0 pass, within 224 float constants and 8 samplers, is a hard budget, and WPF offers nothing newer.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Terminal fidelity trades against surface fidelity. The turnkey ConPTY control is a child HWND that cannot sit inside a rounded, alpha-blended panel; writing the grid renderer on WPF's text stack instead is a multi-week subproject with its own performance ceiling.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] Monochrome emoji in a chat transcript. WPF has no COLR/CPAL support, so parity needs Emoji.Wpf or an equivalent vector re-draw, and that changes text measurement, which feeds layout.

[WPF (.NET 10 / windowsdesktop, MILCore Direct3D 9 rendering) with ShaderEffect + D3DImage/HwndHost interop, DWM system backdrop, optional Windows.UI.Composition island] WPF's own rasterizer, not DirectWrite. Glyph positions will differ from every DirectWrite-based candidate, so all 1029 UI contract records that depend on text metrics must be re-derived against WPF, not merely transcribed.
probes_needed: [WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] Backdrop-to-texture probe (settles the disqualifier definitively, ~1 day): build a WinUI 3 app with Window.SystemBackdrop = DesktopAcrylicBackdrop, place a SpriteVisual with Compositor.CreateBackdropBrush() over it, and attempt to (a) feed that brush into Compositor.CreateEffectFactory with a ComputeSharp PixelShaderEffect<T> in the graph, and (b) capture the brushed visual via Compositor.CreateVisualSurface() into a CompositionSurfaceBrush and read it back. CONFIRMS DISQUALIFICATION if (a) throws or silently drops the effect because PixelShaderEffect is [NoComposition], and (b) yields transparent or the pre-backdrop content. REFUTES only if either produces live desktop pixels usable as a shader input - which would contradict the CreateHostBackdropBrush Remarks and would be the single finding that could reopen this verdict.

[WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK 2.0 (C#/.NET 10, WinRT, Microsoft.UI.Composition, Win2D + ComputeSharp.D2D1)] Fidelity-ceiling probe (~2 days, do this before rejecting outright, because it is what the owner will actually be shown): implement Chrome.swift:178's exact surface - .regular tint at 0.3 opacity, .interactive(), the real shape - twice: once as DesktopAcrylicBackdrop + SystemBackdropElement with a rim-highlight border, and once as a ComputeSharp lensing shader over a Win2D-drawn copy of the Wallpaper layer. adversary.target: Native Win32 + Direct3D 11/12 + Direct2D + DirectComposition (C++), DirectWrite text, HLSL material shaders, Windows.Graphics.Capture for desktop backdrop sampling, ConPTY terminal
adversary.verdict: BREAKS. The stack is competent everywhere except the one criterion OD-0003 made primary: its desktop-backdrop path, Windows.Graphics.Capture, is a privacy-gated screen-recording API, so under an unpackaged Win32 installer the app paints a Windows Screen Capture Indicator border around the user's monitor for its entire runtime, the indicator can be re-forced by any other app capturing the same display, the capability is user/admin-revocable with no fallback in the source to fall back to, and the sampled backdrop is architecturally at least one compositor frame stale relative to the window it is supposed to be refracting.
breaks: CAPTURE INDICATOR, unfixable unpackaged. Violates OD-0003 (exact look, zero guesswork) and constraint 11 (ordinary desktop app, no packaged identity). GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired docs (learn.microsoft.com/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.graphicscapturesession.isborderrequired, introduced 10.0.20348, current through winrt-28000): 'Before the system will disable the colored border ... your app must get consent from the user by calling GraphicsCaptureAccess.RequestAccessAsync, passing in the value GraphicsCaptureAccessKind.Borderless ... To call RequestAccessAsync with GraphicsCaptureAccessKind.Borderless, you must declare the graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder capability in your app's package manifest.' A native Win32 app installed by NSIS/WiX has no package manifest, so it cannot declare uap11:Capability Name="graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder" and cannot call RequestAccessAsync(Borderless). Since Windows 11 22H2 the Screen Capture Indicator draws a bright yellow/orange outline around the captured area; for a monitor-level GraphicsCaptureItem that is the whole monitor. Marrow would therefore run with a yellow rectangle around the user's entire display, permanently, as the price of drawing its own window background. This is the precise opposite of the owner ruling.

EVEN PACKAGED, THE BORDER IS NOT THE APP'S TO CONTROL. Same doc, two further sentences: 'If the user denies access, setting this property to false will succeed, but the value will be ignored and the border will be displayed during subsequent captures' and 'Note that if the IsBorderRequired property is set to true for the same window or display by other apps on the device, the border will be displayed.' So even after shipping MSIX, obtaining the restricted capability and winning a consent prompt, any third-party capture of the same monitor with the default IsBorderRequired=true (Teams, Zoom, Discord, OBS, Snipping Tool, and Parsec, which is installed on the stated target machine as a virtual display adapter) re-enables the border around Marrow's glass. The app's headline visual is hostage to other processes' capture settings.

THE ENTIRE VISUAL SURFACE SITS BEHIND A REVOCABLE PRIVACY PERMISSION, WITH NO FALLBACK TO COPY. Programmatic capture by non-packaged apps is consent-store gated at HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\CapabilityAccessManager\\ConsentStore\\graphicsCaptureProgrammatic\\NonPackaged, which a user or an enterprise policy can set to Deny; GraphicsCaptureAccessKind has a distinct Programmatic member (value 1) alongside Borderless, and GraphicsCaptureSession.IsSupported() is documented as a required pre-flight that can return false on devices that do not meet hardware requirements. If capture is denied or unsupported, every one of the 22 .glassEffect sites has no backdrop. The spec states there is NO NSVisualEffectView or Material fallback anywhere in the Droppy source, so the port would have to invent a degraded material from nothing. Inventing an unrendered material is exactly the guesswork OD-0003 forbids, and the port would have to ship it as the default experience on any locked-down machine.

SELF-CAPTURE: A FORK WITH NO ACCEPTABLE BRANCH. A monitor GraphicsCaptureItem returns the composed desktop including Marrow's own window, so sampling it into Marrow's glass is an infinite mirror. The only suppression is SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) (supported from Windows 10 2004; earlier it degrades to WDA_MONITOR), and it withholds the window from EVERY capture path: GDI BitBlt, DXGI Desktop Duplication, Windows.Graphics.Capture and DWM thumbnails. Taking that branch means the user can never screenshot Marrow with Snipping Tool, never screen-share it in Teams/Zoom/Parsec, and sees blank taskbar, Alt-Tab and Task View thumbnails. It also breaks a spec'd feature: App/Captures (3 files, 1,740 lines: WebsiteCaptures.swift 1,122 lines, TourCaptures, TourCaptures+Hydra, architecture.md lines 216-219) is the app's own ScreenCaptureKit screenshot and film harness that produced the eight tour-*@2x.png assets recorded in OD-0004. Under WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE the port's own harness photographs an empty rectangle. And the exclusion is defeated in RDP sessions, where DWM is not composing, so the mirror returns.

MULTI-WINDOW GLASS IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY ON THIS STACK. Constraint 2 requires floating panels docked beside the chat (three a side on a 16-inch display) plus head panels that pop out on their own, and contract section 10 forbids collapsing them into one page. Each is a separate HWND with its own DirectComposition target and its own WGC session. If the main window is excluded from capture to stop the mirror (previous item), a docked or overlapping panel's glass samples the desktop BEHIND the main window rather than the main window's content, so it refracts the wrong pixels. If the main window is not excluded, the panels and the main window mutually mirror each other. macOS gets this free because WindowServer composites all NSWindows in one z-ordered pass and .glassEffect samples what is genuinely beneath the shape in that pass. Win32/DWM exposes no 'everything below HWND X' layer at all; WGC only hands you the finished desktop. Separately, N independent capture sessions are not frame-synchronised with each other, so adjacent docked panels will tear against one another during a window drag.

BACKDROP LATENCY IS ARCHITECTURAL AND UNTUNABLE, AND IT HITS EXACTLY THE FIELD-EVIDENCE CASE. WGC delivers frames of the ALREADY-COMPOSED desktop via Direct3D11CaptureFramePool/FrameArrived; Marrow then renders with that texture and is itself composed by DWM in the NEXT frame. The backdrop is therefore at minimum one compositor frame stale relative to the window's own position: 16.7ms at 60Hz, 8.3ms at 120Hz. Direct3D11CaptureFramePool.CreateFreeThreaded exists specifically to shave latency by moving FrameArrived off the app thread, which is an admission that latency is the known problem. The stated field evidence for parity is 'edge refraction with visible chromatic fringing where the window border crosses high-contrast desktop content' - i.e. the lensing is judged AT THE MOVING EDGE, which is precisely where a one-frame-stale backdrop slides out from under the border during a drag or live resize. macOS composites the glass and its backdrop in the same pass with zero offset. No shader, no D3D12 path and no GPU closes this; the pixels simply arrive after the fact.

THE BACKDROP DIES ON EVERY DISPLAY TOPOLOGY CHANGE, ON A MACHINE THAT HAS A VIRTUAL DISPLAY ADAPTER. A monitor GraphicsCaptureItem is invalidated on display removal, resolution change or topology change (GraphicsCaptureItem.Closed), requiring the session, frame pool and item to be rebuilt. On the stated target that fires on Parsec connect/disconnect, on RDP attach, on monitor hotplug and on DPI/resolution changes. Each event blanks or freezes the app's entire background until rebuilt. There are also filed reports of GraphicsCaptureItem.Closed simply not firing (robmikh/Win32CaptureSample issue 17), so the port cannot even rely on the notification to rebuild. Indirect display drivers such as Parsec's are exactly the class where per-monitor WGC items are least exercised.

THE ONLY PACKAGING ESCAPE FROM THE BORDER BREAKS CONSTRAINT 4. Accepting MSIX to obtain graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder makes Marrow a packaged app, and child processes inherit the desktop app runtime environment (filesystem write virtualization via wcnfs.sys, environment rewriting) unless every CreateProcessW is fitted with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_DESKTOP_APP_POLICY breakaway. This is not hypothetical for this exact workload - it is filed against this exact class of app: anthropics/claude-code issue 93152 (MSIX desktop app: agent sessions inherit AppData filesystem virtualization, so tools installed from inside a session land in the package LocalCache and are invisible or broken outside the app), issue 62574 (MSIX-packaged Claude Desktop strips PATHEXT to .CPL and empties WINDIR for spawned MCP subprocess shells), issue 91028 (MSIX identity detection breaks sandbox startup). Marrow's entire purpose is supervising 13 provider CLIs with streaming stdio. The fix for the border breaks the product, and MSIX+.appinstaller is also a different update mechanism from constraint 11's stated ordinary Windows installer.

MAIN-THREAD ORDERING (C3) GETS THE LEAST HELP FROM THIS STACK, AND THE STACK PUSHES THE OTHER WAY. architecture.md C3 states 256 @MainActor annotations are a correctness invariant, not a style, and that TokenLedger explicitly skips locking on the strength of it; the sessionEpoch / finishingTurnID / unsentSessionID rules are named as the ones most likely to break. Swift's MainActor is a compiler-enforced serial executor. C++/Win32 has no enforcement at all - thread affinity becomes convention plus review. And the stack's own recommended pattern actively moves work off the UI thread: Direct3D11CaptureFramePool.CreateFreeThreaded is documented as firing FrameArrived on the pool's worker thread rather than the app's thread, which is required for acceptable backdrop latency. So the port must hand-build a MainActor equivalent (message-pumped dispatch queue plus C++20 resume_foreground) and then hand-audit 256 call sites against it, with zero compiler help. This is the one non-glass area where the stack choice is genuinely differentiating and it is differentiating against this candidate.
optimistic: 'Windows.Graphics.Capture can sample desktop content behind the window.' Half true and materially misleading. It samples the whole composed desktop, not the content behind the window: there is no z-order filter, so occluders, always-on-top windows and Marrow's own window are all in the texture, and the only exclusion primitive (WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) is all-or-nothing per window and applies to every capture path on the machine. Correction: WGC gives a screen recording, not a backdrop; every one of the glass sites' semantics has to be reconstructed on top of a recording.

'ConPTY covers the embedded terminal.' Overstated as a like-for-like. SwiftTerm drives a real pty and receives the child's bytes; ConPTY interposes conhost/OpenConsole, which re-renders the client's screen buffer and re-emits VT, so output is normalised rather than passed through, and resize re-wraps through the emulator. ClosePseudoConsole blocked indefinitely on the output pipe until Windows 11 24H2 build 26100 made it return immediately (microsoft/terminal issues 1810, 17489, 4050 lingering conhost.exe; PRs 14041 and 14160 fixing shutdown deadlocks). Correction: the support floor becomes Windows 11 24H2, or the port must carry ClosePseudoConsoleTimeout. Note this is stack-neutral - every Windows stack uses ConPTY - so it is not a reason to prefer a different candidate.

'SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL with group kill is handled by ConPTY plus Job Objects.' It is not expressible for 13 concurrent children from one supervisor. GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent only signals 'a console process group that shares the console associated with the calling process', and AttachConsole is documented as failing with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED because a process can be attached to at most one console at a time. Supervising 13 CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP children therefore requires 13 helper relay processes, or you abandon graceful shutdown for TerminateJobObject, which is SIGKILL-only. Correction, and I concede the point cuts nobody's way: this is a Windows platform limit identical for Electron, Tauri, WinUI and Avalonia, so it is not a differentiator - but any evaluation that implied native C++ makes it tractable was wrong.

'App-drawn caption buttons on the leading edge: full control.' Full responsibility, not full control. WM_NCCALCSIZE frame removal reintroduces the documented maximized-window-covers-the-taskbar behaviour, requiring per-monitor WM_GETMINMAXINFO correction and the NonRudeHWND property for auto-hide taskbars; Windows 11 snap layouts appear only if WM_NCHITTEST returns HTMAXBUTTON over the drawn button, and the flyout then anchors to that rect on the LEFT edge, a placement Microsoft does not test. Correction: this is a real but bounded bug tail, identical to the one Electron already carries, so it is engineering cost rather than a disqualifier.

'DirectWrite handles the first-party type scale.' This one I concede outright and it is the stack's strongest card: IDWriteTextLayout gives per-cluster metrics, hit testing, custom line breaking and per-range drawing effects, which is more measurement control than a web or XAML layer offers, and D2D path geometry makes a mapped SF Symbols replacement practical at arbitrary size and weight. The residual risk (SF Pro is non-redistributable, Segoe UI Variable has different metrics, so 430+ system-font sites reflow) is stack-neutral and already recorded as PA-0012/PA-0013. The stack does not fail on constraints 7 or 8. It fails on constraint 1, which OD-0003 made primary.

'Live resize with held springs is straightforward.' UNRESOLVED and currently unprobeable on the stated machine. The sizing modal loop entered at WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE runs the system's own message loop, so per-frame spring stepping must be driven from a timer installed for its duration, and every WM_SIZE requires releasing all back-buffer references and calling IDXGISwapChain::ResizeBuffers. Stacked on a monitor-sized WGC session whose frames arrive free-threaded, this is the most expensive frame in the app occurring at the highest frequency, on an AMD integrated GPU. PROBE THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a minimal Win32 + DirectComposition + D3D11 harness that opens a monitor-level WGC session, runs a gaussian-plus-refraction HLSL pass over a 1320x860 window, and records frame times while dragging across a high-contrast wallpaper, measured separately on the iGPU output and on the Parsec virtual adapter, with IsBorderRequired left at its default so the indicator behaviour is observed directly. That probe cannot be run on this machine today: MSVC, cmake, Rust and the .NET SDK are all absent and only Windows SDK headers 10.0.26100 are present, so the candidate's central claim is unverified here until VS Build Tools are installed via winget.
