adversary.verdict: BREAKS. Qt can build a convincing custom material over the app's own wallpaper layer, but the primary criterion under OD-0003 is the field-observed appearance where the window is nearly transparent over the DESKTOP with desktop widgets legible and chromatic fringing at the refracting edge, and neither Qt nor Win32 hands an application the desktop pixels behind its own window; the only route that does (Windows.Graphics.Capture) forces MSIX packaging, a consent prompt, a capture border the app cannot fully suppress, and a self-exclusion that makes Marrow invisible to every screenshot and screen share it runs alongside. Secondary but independently disqualifying: QProcess cannot reproduce C4's graceful SIGTERM of console children, cannot do process-group kill, cannot carry a ConPTY, and Qt has no Windows terminal emulator to stand in for SwiftTerm 1.20.0.
breaks: C1 / OD-0003, the load-bearing one: Qt's effects pipeline samples the app's scene graph, never the desktop. ShaderEffect/ShaderEffectSource and Qt Quick Effects MultiEffect take a Qt Quick item as source; there is no Qt API that yields the composited desktop content behind a QQuickWindow. Dropping to direct Win32 does not fix it, because both documented DWM backdrop APIs are closed to the app: DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow's own Remarks state 'Beginning with Windows 8, calling this function doesn't result in the blur effect, due to a style change in the way windows are rendered' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dwmapi/nf-dwmapi-dwmenableblurbehindwindow), and DWM_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE (min. Windows 11 Build 22621) is explicitly a 'system-drawn backdrop material' - DWMSBT_MAINWINDOW is Mica, DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW is Desktop Acrylic - composited by DWM behind the window with no pixel handback and no shader hook, and the doc warns 'The material effect might change with future Windows releases' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dwmapi/ne-dwmapi-dwm_systembackdrop_type). Mica/Acrylic have no lensing, no specular edge and no .interactive() pointer deformation, so substituting one is precisely the flatten that PA-0001 and contract section 10 forbid - and its appearance would drift with Windows servicing, which exact parity cannot absorb.

The only desktop-sampling route on Windows carries a capture indicator the app cannot unilaterally remove. To get real backdrop pixels you must use Windows.Graphics.Capture. GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired's Remarks: 'Before the system will disable the colored border around the a window or display that is being captured, your app must get consent from the user by calling GraphicsCaptureAccess.RequestAccessAsync, passing in the value GraphicsCaptureAccessKind.Borderless, which displays a prompt to the user' and 'To call RequestAccessAsync with GraphicsCaptureAccessKind.Borderless, you must declare the graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder capability in your app's package manifest' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.graphicscapturesession.isborderrequired). Package manifest means MSIX package identity - a plain NSIS/Inno/MSI build cannot declare it at all, which collides with derived constraint 11. Worse, the same Remarks add: 'if the IsBorderRequired property is set to true for the same window or display by other apps on the device, the border will be displayed.' Any concurrent OBS, Teams, Discord or Snipping Tool capture of that monitor puts a colored border around the whole screen for as long as Marrow is open, and Marrow has no way to override it. graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder and graphicsCaptureProgrammatic are general-use, not restricted, capabilities (no Store approval needed), so the gate is packaging and consent, not certification - but the gate is still real.

Self-capture feedback, and the documented fix makes the app unshareable. Capturing the monitor includes Marrow's own window, producing recursive hall-of-mirrors feedback in the glass. The only documented exclusion is SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE): 'The window is displayed only on a monitor. Everywhere else, the window does not appear at all' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowdisplayaffinity). Applied to the 1320x860 main window, the 780x580 settings window, up to six docked floating panels and every popped-out head panel, Marrow becomes invisible in Teams, Zoom, OBS, Snipping Tool and every screen recording for its entire run. For a tool whose users demo agent runs this is a product regression the glass parity is buying. The same page also notes the mechanism 'works only when the Desktop Window Manager (DWM) is composing the desktop.'

C4: the graceful half of SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL does not exist through QProcess. Qt 6.11 QProcess docs: terminate() on Windows 'posts a WM_CLOSE message to all top-level windows of the process and then to the main thread', and 'Console applications on Windows that do not run an event loop ... can only be terminated by calling kill()', where kill() 'uses TerminateProcess' (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qprocess.html). All 13 provider CLIs are console programs with no message loop, so Shell.swift:110-118's SIGTERM, one-second gap, then SIGKILL, and StdioProcess.swift:114-120's stdin-close + SIGTERM + 3 s deadline, both collapse to an immediate hard TerminateProcess on every interrupt - no session flush, no cleanup, on tools that write session state. The POSIX analogue is GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT), which requires a shared console; the same QProcess page notes 'The called process inherits the console window of the calling process', and a /SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS Qt GUI app has none to inherit.

C4: process-group kill has no QProcess route. getpgid(pid)==pid group kill maps to a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, which must be assigned before the child runs any code. QProcess::setCreateProcessArgumentsModifier exposes only flags and a STARTUPINFOW* (the documented example touches args->flags and args->startupInfo->dwFlags) and hands back no PROCESS_INFORMATION, so CREATE_SUSPENDED + AssignProcessToJobObject + ResumeThread is not expressible. Assigning after QProcess::processId() returns leaves a window in which a grandchild spawns outside the job. Either you write your own process class and lose QProcess's overlapped Windows pipe reader, or you accept orphaned agent subprocesses across 13 concurrent supervisions.

Constraint 3, the embedded terminal: ConPTY cannot ride QProcess, and there is no Qt terminal emulator to port. ConPTY requires CreatePseudoConsole plus a STARTUPINFOEXW carrying PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_PSEUDOCONSOLE and EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT; QProcess offers a STARTUPINFOW pointer and installs its own STARTF_USESTDHANDLES pipe handles, so the pty path means abandoning QProcess for that child. Separately, SwiftTerm 1.20.0 is a full VT emulator plus renderer plus scrollback plus selection. Qt's only comparable widget, QTermWidget, describes itself as 'compatible with BSD, Linux and OS X' (https://github.com/lxqt/qtermwidget) and has no Windows support; ptyqt supplies the pty only, not the emulator. Contract section 10 forbids replacing the terminal with an external one, so this is a from-scratch xterm-compatible emulator in QML on top of hand-rolled ConPTY - scope an optimistic evaluation would not have priced.

Reader threads: QSocketNotifier is sockets-only on Windows, and ConPTY pipes are synchronous. Qt's QSocketNotifier documentation states you cannot use it to receive notifications on stdin on Windows because Windows does not send single-object notifications on it, and on Windows the class is oriented to network sockets. The anonymous pipes returned by CreatePseudoConsole are not opened for overlapped I/O, so they cannot be driven by QWinEventNotifier either. Every pty and every non-QProcess child therefore needs a dedicated blocking reader thread, each marshalling chunks across queued connections into the GUI thread - which is also the QML engine thread that must hold C12's 45 ms flush window and 45/90/150 ms tiers while 13 CLIs stream.

C3 versus Qt's own threading model. Qt Quick's scene graph docs state 'The threaded renderer is currently used by default on Windows with Direct3D 11', with the GUI thread explicitly blocked across the sync point (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtquick-visualcanvas-scenegraph.html). The only way to feed a captured desktop frame into a ShaderEffect is QNativeInterface::QSGD3D11Texture::fromNative, documented as 'must be called on the scene graph rendering thread' and returning null before the scene graph is initialized (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qnativeinterface-qsgd3d11texture.html). So the entire backdrop pipeline runs on a thread outside the 256 @MainActor ordering rules the source depends on, while the sync-point block introduces a GUI-thread stall the macOS app never had - directly against architecture.md section 5.6 (flushDeltas before every completion handler, finishingTurnID claimed before the first suspension, the AppModel.sync/write split).

Constraint 8, iconography: Qt's SVG renderer is not a general SVG renderer. Qt supports 'the static features of the SVG 1.2 Tiny profile'; the <clipPath> element 'is not supported'; and the extended features (mask element, filter primitives) 'are currently only supported by the software rasterizer and not the hardware-accelerated renderer in VectorImage or svgtoqml' (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/svgextensions.html). A mapped 181-glyph replacement for the SF Symbol sites drawn from any modern icon library will silently mis-render wherever it uses clip-path, and in Qt Quick's hardware path loses masks and filters entirely - at arbitrary sizes and weights, which is exactly what constraint 8 asks the stack to make practical.

Constraint 7, text: no Qt Quick render type satisfies both the first-party type scale and the animation. The default Text.QtRendering is a distance field that 'uses more memory and will exhibit rendering artifacts at large sizes', with renderTypeQuality existing because the rasterizer 'may give artifacts at large text sizes, such as sharp corners looking rounder than they should'. Text.NativeRendering is the one that matches platform metrics, but the docs warn to select it only if you 'do not require advanced features such as transformation of the text', and that 'Using such features in combination with the NativeRendering render type will lend poor and sometimes pixelated results' (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtquick-text.html). The StreamVeil reveal, the genie distortion and the spring-animated panels all transform text, and text metrics feed layout, so the 430+ system-font sites and 50 monospaced sites must be decided site by site between correct metrics and correct animation - a measured parity loss either way.

Licensing and toolchain. Under LGPLv3 the port must ship the Qt DLL set with relink capability (or the app's source), plus Qt copyright and licence text displayed prominently in the UI (https://www.qt.io/development/open-source-lgpl-obligations); the alternative is a paid commercial licence. Qt's official Windows binaries from 6.8 onward are MSVC 2022 builds. Probed on this machine: cl, cmake, ninja and qmake are all absent, there is no C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio directory and no C:\Qt. Not one line of this stack can be compiled or probed today, so every claim the evaluation made about it is currently unverified on the target hardware.
optimistic: 'Qt can render Liquid Glass because MultiEffect gives blur and ShaderEffect gives arbitrary custom shaders.' Correct for the glass sites that sit over the app's own wallpaper layer (UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift); false for the sites the field evidence shows over the desktop, because both APIs sample a Qt Quick item, not the desktop. MultiEffect also caps blurMax at a 'meaningful range ... from 2 (subtle blur) to 64 (high blur)' and warns 'Blur and shadow are the heaviest effects. With these, prefer increasing blurMultiplier over blurMax and avoid using source items which animate' - the glass in this app sits over a live streaming transcript, which is an animating source by definition, at a window-sized surface that Chrome.swift:219 already records as a full-window backdrop sample every frame.

'Windows 11 Mica/Acrylic via DwmSetWindowAttribute gets close enough.' It is system-drawn and unshaderable, has no refraction, specular edge or pointer-tracking deformation, and its own documentation says 'The material effect might change with future Windows releases' - a parity target cannot be defined by a material Microsoft reserves the right to restyle. Correction: this is PA-0001's forbidden flatten, one step less flat.

'Screen capture solves the backdrop problem.' Only with MSIX package identity, a user consent prompt on first run, a capture border that any other capturing app on the same display can force back on, one frame of latency between the desktop content and its refraction, and a WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE self-exclusion that makes the app invisible to all screen sharing. Correction: this is a trade, not a solution, and each leg of it needs owner acceptance.

'QProcess covers subprocess supervision.' It covers streaming stdio well, via overlapped pipe reads on the pipes it creates. It does not cover graceful termination of console children (documented as kill()-only, i.e. TerminateProcess), process-group kill (no PROCESS_INFORMATION, no CREATE_SUSPENDED path through setCreateProcessArgumentsModifier), or ConPTY attachment (STARTUPINFOW, not STARTUPINFOEXW).
'SwiftTerm maps onto a Qt terminal widget.' QTermWidget states BSD, Linux and OS X. Correction: the terminal is net-new work, not a dependency swap.

'Direct Win32/DXGI calls fill whatever Qt does not wrap.' The gap that matters here is a Windows platform gap, not a Qt wrapper gap. DWM composites the desktop and does not hand applications the pixels behind their own window; dropping below Qt does not conjure them. Qt is if anything better placed than a web stack here, because QSGD3D11Texture::fromNative can adopt a capture texture - it just cannot obtain one without the capture regime above.

'The threaded render loop is a performance win.' It is also a new correctness surface. Default on Windows/D3D11, with a documented GUI-thread block across sync and a rendering thread that now owns the backdrop pipeline - measured against 256 @MainActor annotations and the ordering invariants in architecture.md section 5.6.

What I could not break, stated plainly so the comparison is fair: QML/Qt Quick genuinely does give a fully custom material - blur, specular edge treatment, refraction and .interactive() pointer-tracking deformation - over app-drawn content, and the Metal Genie shader ports to a .qsb ShaderEffect. Multiple native top-level windows, docking panels and pop-out heads are ordinary Qt. App-drawn caption buttons on the leading edge are achievable with WS_THICKFRAME|WS_CAPTION plus WM_NCCALCSIZE and WM_NCHITTEST returning HTMAXBUTTON so Windows 11 Snap Layouts still open (the approach QWindowKit ships), and Qt 6 has startSystemMove/startSystemResize. Precise text measurement and line breaking via QTextLayout on HarfBuzz is a strength, not a weakness. Packaging as MSI/MSIX with WinVerifyTrust satisfies constraint 11 on its own terms. The kill is the desktop backdrop plus the process and terminal layer, not the UI toolkit's expressiveness.

UNRESOLVED, with the probes that would settle each: (1) Does Qt's D3D11 RHI back a translucent QQuickWindow through DirectComposition? Qt documents the DComp composition swapchain for the D3D12 backend; I found no equivalent statement for D3D11 in the 6.11 docs. Probe: build the Qt rhiwindow example with QSurfaceFormat alphaBufferSize 8 and QQuickWindow::setDefaultAlphaBuffer(true) under QSG_RHI_BACKEND=d3d11, over a patterned desktop, and screenshot. (2) Do QML spring animations keep ticking through a Win32 live-resize modal loop (constraint 9)? Qt's event dispatcher installs a message hook, so I will not assert the freeze without evidence. Probe: a QQuickWindow with a looping NumberAnimation, logging frame timestamps across WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE/WM_EXITSIZEMOVE while dragging the frame. (3) Does Windows.Graphics.Capture display capture initialize at all with this machine's Parsec virtual display adapter present, and does Qt Quick fall back to software rendering on it? Qt's Windows graphics page notes automatic software fallback 'when the drivers do not provide a sufficient level of D3D11 functionality ... typically in virtual machines that do not have proper GPU acceleration and passthrough'; a software-rendered scene cannot run the glass shaders at all. Probe: GraphicsCaptureSession::IsSupported() plus IGraphicsCaptureItemInterop::CreateForMonitor per HMONITOR, logging adapter LUID, then a Qt Quick scene with QSG_INFO=1. (4) Frame cost of a full-monitor capture plus blur plus 22 refraction sites on the AMD integrated GPU. Probe: 22 ShaderEffect glass shapes over a WGC-sourced QSGD3D11Texture, measured with QSG_RENDER_TIMING=1 at 1320x860 and maximised.

adversary.target: Electron 44.x (Chromium + Node) + TypeScript, with node-pty/xterm.js and electron-builder NSIS + electron-updater, for the exact-parity Windows port of Droppy Code (Marrow)
adversary.verdict: BREAKS. Electron can render lensed glass over content the page itself paints (verified in the owner's own repo, Chromium 152), but it cannot render any custom material over the DESKTOP, which is precisely where the macOS field evidence puts the hardest glass case, so it fails the primary weighted criterion OD-0003 on its own terms; four further requirements (non-activating all-workspaces MCP panels, the conditional SIGTERM/SIGKILL group-kill, FSEvents event-loss flags, and the four PR-UPDATE feed requirements) are not translations but unimplementable in this stack without native addons that void the stack's premise. Attacks that FAILED: node-pty is fine (1.1.0 ships win32-x64 and win32-arm64 ConPTY prebuilds at C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds/, so no MSVC is needed and the missing toolchain on this machine is a non-issue), Web Audio covers the runtime-synthesised chimes, and edge refraction via feDisplacementMap in backdrop-filter genuinely works.
breaks: GLASS OVER THE DESKTOP IS UNREACHABLE, AND THAT IS THE PRIMARY CRITERION (violates C1 / OD-0003 / PA-0001). Electron offers exactly two paths and both fail for desktop-backed surfaces. (a) backgroundMaterial: the shipped Electron 44.4.1 typings at C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:3268-3278 describe it as the window's 'system-drawn background material, including behind the non-client area', supported only on 'Windows 11 22H2 and up'. System-drawn means DWM composites it BENEATH Chromium's surface; the renderer never receives those pixels, so no specular edge, no lensing and no pointer-tracked deformation can be computed against them. The entire API surface is a five-value enum ('auto'|'none'|'mica'|'acrylic'|'tabbed') with no tint, no blur radius, no opacity and no per-element application. (b) backdrop-filter samples only the backdrop root, i.e. content painted by the page; over the desktop there is nothing in the backdrop root to sample. The field evidence the port must match (desktop widgets LEGIBLE through the window, chromatic fringing where the border crosses high-contrast desktop content) requires live desktop pixels inside the app's own shader. Neither path supplies them, and E:/Droppy/port/porting/platform_adaptations.md:42-48 already records that Mica and Acrylic have 'none of the lensing, specular edge, or interactive deformation' and that substituting Acrylic is exactly what contract section 10 forbids.

ONE WINDOW-WIDE ENUM CANNOT EXPRESS 22 PER-SITE MATERIALS (violates C1 and contract section 10). backgroundMaterial applies to the whole window. The contract requires 22 glassEffect/GlassEffectContainer sites in 18 files, each with its own shape, corner radius and tint: 0.3 alpha on every chrome capsule and circle, 0.22 dark / 0.16 light on sheets and the floating panel, 0.1 warning tint on RequestCards, 0.55/0.32 white on the ChatView circle (E:/Droppy/port/porting/port_impacts.md:334 and platform_adaptations.md:20-28, which says explicitly 'Three different numbers, do not collapse'). The system material has no per-surface form at all, so every one of the 22 sites that sits over the desktop must fall back to the page-painted approximation, which reintroduces the flattening the contract prohibits.

THE OWNER'S OWN ELECTRON 44.4.1 APP HAS FAILED TO SETTLE THIS QUESTION ACROSS TWO VERIFICATION BLOCKS (direct field evidence against the evaluation). C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/PROJECT_STATE.md:88 records 'The glass looked flat in the screenshot; whether transparency effects, Energy saver or Electron's material caused it is open'; line 92 still says 'Open: acrylic still needs a check with a colorful window behind and a capture that keeps focus (Alt+PrtScn)'; line 110 has that check queued as a next action. Its docs/LIMITATIONS.md:92-95 ships the conclusion to users: 'Electron's system material has known Windows issues (for example a flat gray window while Energy saver is on); choose None in Settings, Appearance if it looks wrong. Whether acrylic shows the desktop on the owner's PC is still being checked.' A stack whose primary-criterion feature ships with a turn-it-off-if-it-looks-wrong switch cannot satisfy OD-0003's 'zero guesswork'.

THE MATERIAL HAS THREE RUNTIME STATES ON WINDOWS WHERE MACOS HAS ONE (violates contract section 10's 'do not flatten translucent material into a solid fill'). The existing app must poll the registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize /v EnableTransparency (C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/src/main/app/windowAppearance.ts:37-49) and swap to painted glass when the user's Transparency effects switch is off (same file, usesMaterial() at :52-54), and it separately reports a flat gray window under Energy saver. So parity depends on two OS settings the app does not control, and the documented fallback IS the flattening the contract forbids, on supported configurations, by design.

THE NON-ACTIVATING MCP PANELS CANNOT BE BUILT (violates C2 and contract section 10's 'do not reduce multiple panels to one page'). E:/Droppy/port/porting/critiques/settings-usage-tour-diff-terminal.md:49 specifies MCPKeyPanel and MCPSetupPanel as NSPanels with styleMask [.nonactivatingPanel,.fullSizeContentView,.titled,.closable] and collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces,.fullScreenAuxiliary]; port_impacts.md:428 already carries that forward as 'frameless non-activating utility panel for both MCP panels (all workspaces, no window controls)'. Electron 44.4.1 implements neither attribute: setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces is annotated '@platform darwin,linux' with 'This API does nothing on Windows' (electron.d.ts:3595-3601), and the only activation control is focusable, where 'On Windows setting focusable: false also implies setting skipTaskbar: true' (electron.d.ts:3881-3887) and the window then cannot take keyboard focus at all. These are panels the user types an MCP secret into. .nonactivatingPanel means 'becomes key and accepts typing without activating the app'; Electron's binary gives you either a focus-stealing normal window or a window you cannot type in. There is no WS_EX_NOACTIVATE anywhere in the API surface.

LEADING-EDGE APP-DRAWN CAPTION BUTTONS FORCE frame:false AND COST SNAP LAYOUTS (violates C2 and requirement 2). TitleBarOverlay exposes only color, symbolColor and height (electron.d.ts:24084-24104) and the overlay is OS-drawn at the inline end; there is no side or position option. The owner's existing app took exactly that path and therefore has its caption buttons on the RIGHT (windowAppearance.ts:65-66, titleBarStyle:'hidden' plus titleBarOverlay), already a deviation from the spec's leading-edge geometry, whose constants are derived and waiting: collapsedTrafficLightTop 21, trafficLightPitch 23, trafficLightsWidth 60, trafficLightsFitWidth 88, titlebarHeight 44 (critiques/shell-chrome-and-theme.md:71). Placing them on the left requires frame:false and hand-drawn controls, and Electron exposes no WM_NCHITTEST hook, so the window cannot return HTMAXBUTTON and Windows 11 Snap Layouts on maximize-hover do not appear. That is a native-behavior regression the parity contract does not authorize trading away.

THE SIGTERM-THEN-SIGKILL GRACE SECOND DOES NOT EXIST ON NODE (violates C4 and requirement 4). E:/Droppy/port/porting/architecture.md records the behavior as load-bearing: 'the whole process group is killed when the child is its own group leader, otherwise only the child... This is a real, reproducible behavior, not an accident to normalize away.' Node documents that on Windows, where POSIX signals do not exist, SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGKILL all cause the target to be 'killed forcefully and abruptly', so child.kill('SIGTERM') is an immediate TerminateProcess and the one second in which a provider CLI flushes its last JSONL line is fictional; whatever the macOS build emits in that second is simply lost. The owner's own Electron app has already normalized the behavior away in exactly the manner the spec forbids: C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/src/main/process/kill.ts:7 reads 'Kills a process and its descendants. On Windows `taskkill /T /F`; on POSIX the process group, then the pid', i.e. an unconditional hard tree kill replacing a kill conditioned on getpgid(pid)==pid. taskkill /T also walks the tree as enumerated, so a grandchild that re-parents between enumeration and kill survives; the correct primitive is a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, which Node cannot create without a native addon.

THE FSEVENTS EVENT-LOSS FLAGS HAVE NO EXPRESSION IN NODE, SO THE REQUIREMENT IS BLOCKED, NOT TRANSLATED (violates C6 and requirement 5). architecture.md C6 requires kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents | kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer, realpath(3) resolution, cookie files under the git directory to order events, and three event-loss flags, capped at 32 watches. Node's fs.watch on Windows wraps ReadDirectoryChangesW and surfaces neither the buffer-overflow condition (ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR) nor any must-rescan signal, and Node's own caveats state the API 'is not 100% consistent across platforms'. You therefore cannot implement 'we lost events, rescan' at all; you can only fail to know. This one is Electron-specific rather than Windows-general: a stack that can call ReadDirectoryChangesW directly, or use Rust's notify, does see the overflow error. Recovering it in Electron means a native addon, which is the cost the stack was chosen to avoid.

transparent:true IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH FOR THE GLASS (violates C1 and C2 together). electron.d.ts:4057-4062 states transparent 'On Windows, does not work unless the window is frameless', so choosing it also forfeits the native frame; and a transparent window has no DWM backdrop at all, so you trade the system material for nothing while the page still cannot read desktop pixels. It is also mutually exclusive with backgroundMaterial in practice, which is why the owner's app sets backgroundColor '#00000000' with the material and never sets transparent (windowAppearance.ts:67-69). Against requirement 9 this compounds: the main window is 1320x860, resizable, content minimum 860x560, with spring animations that must keep ticking through live resize. UNRESOLVED, and the probe that settles it: build a frameless transparent Electron 44.4.1 window on this AMD integrated GPU, drive a rAF spring, drag-resize it, and count dropped frames against the same spring in a non-transparent window.

PER-FRAME FULL-WINDOW BACKDROP SAMPLING IS ALREADY RATIONED IN THE OWNER'S OWN IMPLEMENTATION (violates requirement 12). The lensing that does work is documented in C:/Users/omera/Downloads/Claude outputs/agent-workbench/src/renderer/components/glass.tsx:6-20, including its cost: 'Each one is a filter the compositor runs on every frame the backdrop changes, so it belongs on the few surfaces that sit over moving content and earn it.' The parity target is 22 sites including a window-sized surface that architecture.md:834 identifies as 'a full-window backdrop sample every frame', over a live streaming transcript, while 13 provider CLIs are supervised. A reference filter (feImage + feDisplacementMap inside backdrop-filter) forces a render surface and is the most expensive backdrop path Chromium has. Probe: 22 concurrent lensed surfaces at 1320x860 over a streaming transcript on this GPU, measured in frames, before any stack decision is signed.

electron-updater CANNOT SATISFY THE DERIVED UPDATE REQUIREMENTS (violates requirement 11 and four named requirements). PR-UPDATE-005 in E:/Droppy/port/porting/spec/UPDATE.json demands 'Exactly one GET to https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/86415974/releases?per_page=20 with no token and no credentials'; PR-UPDATE-019 and PR-UPDATE-020 demand the literal strings "Couldn't reach GitLab." (with U+2019, not ASCII) and 'GitLab answered with HTTP <status>.'; PR-UPDATE-027 demands an all-or-nothing lenient decode of six named fields where any type mismatch reports the reach-failure message. electron-updater ships providers for GitHub, Bitbucket, Keygen, S3/Spaces, generic and Snap Store; there is no GitLab provider, and it issues its own requests, retries, caching and error text, so using it for the check violates all four outright. Using it only for the install step needs a latest.yml plus blockmap channel layout that the GitLab Releases API does not serve. What remains is hand-rolled download plus launching the NSIS installer, at which point electron-updater is not in the stack and signature verification is whatever you write yourself. The verification it does provide is a PowerShell Get-AuthenticodeSignature subject-string comparison against a configured publisherName, skipped entirely when publisherName is unset, and this project has no certificate at all today (PROJECT_STATE.md:31 'Marrow's own updater still needs a release host and a certificate'; CLAUDE.md 'The installer is unsigned and the docs say so').

MAIN-ACTOR CONFINEMENT BECOMES A MULTI-PROCESS DISTRIBUTED PROBLEM, WHICH THE SPEC PREDICTED (violates C3 and contract section 9's 'least unnecessary semantic translation'). architecture.md C3: '256 @MainActor annotations; exactly two actors; TokenLedger explicitly skips locking on the strength of it. Any stack whose UI thread model differs (a renderer process separate from a logic process, say) must reintroduce the ordering guarantees listed in section 5.6 by hand, and the sessionEpoch / finishingTurnID / unsentSessionID rules are the ones most likely to break.' Electron is precisely that stack, and worse than the one-renderer case: C2 requires a main window, a separate settings window, up to three floating panels a side and head panels that pop out, so state is replicated across a dozen renderer processes reached by asynchronous IPC and structured-clone copies. TokenLedger's no-lock assumption is then underwritten by nothing. The concrete class of defect: a streamed token forwarded from main to renderer while the user edits a sent message leaves the renderer's optimistic state and main's authoritative state divergent for a round trip, with unsentSessionID read on both sides; in Swift both reads happen in one actor turn and the interleaving cannot occur.

CLAIM: 'SIGTERM then SIGKILL with a one-second gap maps onto Windows.' CORRECTION: it does not map, it evaporates. Node documents Windows signal delivery as unconditional forceful termination for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGKILL alike, so there is no grace window and no flush. The owner's code already concedes this by replacing the whole sequence with taskkill /T /F (src/main/process/kill.ts:7), which additionally kills unconditionally where the source kills the group only when getpgid(pid)==pid. Two distinct behaviors normalized into one, in the one area architecture.md marks 'not an accident to normalize away'.

CLAIM: 'multiple BrowserWindows cover the floating and head panels.' CORRECTION: they cover geometry and nothing else. The two attributes the spec actually names for the MCP panels, non-activating and canJoinAllSpaces, are both absent from Electron on Windows: setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces 'does nothing on Windows' (electron.d.ts:3597) and the only activation control, focusable:false, also forces skipTaskbar and removes keyboard focus entirely from a panel whose purpose is typing a secret into it.

CLAIM: 'app-drawn caption buttons on the leading edge are straightforward with titleBarOverlay.' CORRECTION: TitleBarOverlay carries color, symbolColor and height and nothing else (electron.d.ts:24084-24104); the overlay is OS-drawn at the inline end and cannot be moved. The owner's shipping app proves the outcome: its buttons are on the right. The alternative, frame:false with hand-drawn controls, gives up Windows 11 Snap Layouts because Electron exposes no WM_NCHITTEST hook.
